title: Build the first ontology-governed Essays writing runtime
outcome: Deliver one usable local Essays runtime and clean frontend, based on Whisper and constructed through CyberAlchemy v2 product and capability meaning plus DomainSpec v2 system generation, in which a writer can create, develop, review, revise, and preserve an essay without surrendering intent, evidence, or lifecycle authority to the tool.
rationale: Whisper currently defines a governed composition lifecycle but does not provide an integrated product runtime and focused writing interface. Essays should turn that capability into a project-owned product whose meaning is explicit before implementation, whose open-source substrate is deliberately bounded, and whose system model and implementation are traceable through CAV2-D65 rather than hand-aligned after construction.
scope: one Essays product thesis and bounded first-user writing journey
one definition set covering product, writing, capability, lifecycle, evidence, review, and authority concepts
one product ontology and one Whisper-derived capability ontology with explicit ownership, source, confidence, lifecycle, and residue
one source-first open-source writing software comparison and an owner-selected reuse boundary
one DomainSpec-v2 source package compiled into a generated graph and system ontology
one Project-owned CAV2-D65 ConstructionBinding joining meaning, DomainSpec, implementation, conformance, and runtime evidence
one local runtime and clean frontend for drafting, structured composition state, review feedback, revision, and artifact persistence
unit, integration, generation, deterministic replay, accessibility, and browser acceptance evidence
exclusions: multi-tenant accounts, billing, hosted synchronization, social features, or production deployment
feature parity with the selected open-source writing system
hidden model inference treated as author intent or accepted editorial judgment
canonical promotion of definitions or ontology claims by runtime success
ConstructionBinding registration before all CAV2-D65 stages and their exact evidence are complete
owner_route: Essays Project owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus Whisper capability owner plus DomainSpec v2 owner plus Essays runtime owner

success_conditions.statement: Essays has one schema-valid CAV2-D60 Project and one linked CAV2-D59 Goal with a bounded product outcome and separate owner routes.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: The Project and Goal close bidirectionally, appear in the Goal ontology view, remain authority_effect none, and do not claim achievement by record creation.

success_conditions.statement: The Essays product thesis, definitions, product ontology, and Whisper-derived capability ontology close around one first-user writing journey.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: Machine-readable packages validate exact sources, typed relations, ownership, lifecycle, confidence, residue, and authority ceilings without collapsing product meaning into capability or UI structure.

success_conditions.statement: One open-source writing substrate is selected through explicit license, architecture, feature, provenance, removal, and replacement criteria.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: A source-backed comparison and owner selection identify reusable components, excluded features, license obligations, upstream notices, and a rollback path; no source code is imported before this evidence closes.

success_conditions.statement: Essays crosses the CAV2-D65 construction sequence from definitions and product/capability ontology through DomainSpec v2 to a generated system ontology and implementation.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: A complete Project-owned ConstructionBinding names exact definition, product ontology, business or capability ontology, DomainSpec source, compiler, compiled graph, system ontology, implementation, conformance, and runtime-evidence identities.

success_conditions.statement: A writer can complete the bounded Whisper-derived lifecycle in a clean local frontend backed by the Essays runtime.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: Browser and runtime evidence covers project creation, intent capture, draft persistence, composition state, review comments, targeted revision, validation, explicit unresolved residue, and export without hidden authority transitions.

success_conditions.statement: The same admitted DomainSpec source deterministically reconstructs the system graph and the implementation remains conformant to its accepted system ontology.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: Two-run generation identity, negative drift cases, conformance tests, runtime receipts, accessibility checks, and browser acceptance all pass against the exact implementation bytes.

evidence_requirements: Whisper source meaning must remain distinct from Essays product decisions and runtime implementation.
Product, capability, system, bridge, implementation, and runtime-evidence claims must retain separate identities and owner routes.
Open-source reuse must preserve license text, provenance, notices, modification boundaries, and removal reversibility.
Generated ontology and passing validation must not imply owner acceptance, product value, publication, deployment, or production readiness.
The first frontend must optimize the bounded writing journey rather than inherit unrelated upstream product surfaces.
target_horizon: first local validated writing vertical; no deployment deadline

revision_history.change: Created the proposed Essays Project and first runtime Goal before product ontology, open-source selection, DomainSpec construction, or implementation.

challenge_route: Challenge the desired product outcome through the Essays Project owner, CyberAlchemy ontology implications through the product and ontology owners, Whisper-derived capability meaning through the Whisper capability owner, construction claims through the DomainSpec v2 owner, upstream reuse through license review, and runtime or frontend evidence through the Essays runtime owner.
